scene.title: All Souls
scene.location: Our Lady of Mercy, Daly City → Holy Cross Cemetery, Colma, Mon Nov 2, 4 p.m. to dusk

scenes.title: A Woman Made of Lamps
scenes.location: The bulk, above a garden in Daly City (Arenya, dreaming). Sunday night, 2:40 a.m.
scenes.summary: In a shared dream in the bulk above her parents' Daly City garden, Arenya watches her aunt Susmithaa, the host of the Sowri line's light spirit, take the form of a woman made of lamps as a faceless four-man collection team draws a magnetic net that snuffs her flames. Abernathy fights at Susmithaa's side as her squire; his lantern strike fails and his light gutters, but he shields the single flame Arenya reaches for and holds. In that moment his voice slips briefly out of cockney into something old: "keep it lit, child." Arenya tries to pin the man in the light grey jacket from her investigation wall and fails. She keeps only the words "left pocket", and his net's filament "counts" her, leaving a cold coin-sized spot on the inside of her right wrist. Susmithaa pours all her remaining light into Arenya's flame. The collection catches only ash, and her last words are a charge: something old is waking, the doors will open, keep it lit, go with all the light you can carry, and look after Abernathy ("He'll say he's looking after you. He's lying"). Abernathy is torn loose and bound to Arenya, and Susmithaa's body collapses by the curry-leaf tree. Arenya wakes at 3:19 a.m. with a warm, clenched fist; Abernathy is filling her kettle and warns her in private to hide the hand and leave the wrist mark alone. At 3:20 Amma calls: Susmithaa is dead at Seton, her window lamp went out with oil still in it, and a polite American in a suit reached the hospital before the family and asked whether Susmithaa had a niece.

scenes.title: Woke
scenes.location: A grey sedan on a quiet residential street in Daly City, 2:52 a.m., half a block from the Sowri house
scenes.summary: Caleb Strand wakes for real in Team Four's grey sedan at 2:52 a.m., half a block from the Sowri house. His Crown implant is burnt but live, and the containment canister at his feet reads "full" but holds only ash. He keeps his face flat and reports the collection to the handler Shepherd (Deception 18). He passes off his still-extended filament as a "residual tether" and folds it back along the line instead of cutting it. That leaves Arenya's wrist tag masked, faint and findable only by him, and the cost is the first bite of Vesper withdrawal. At the on-ramp light on the way to Drop Two, he unbuckles and bails with the canister (Acrobatics 18). The Crown-flat team doesn't pursue; they drive off to report. Over the Crown, Shepherd calls him "Caleb" for the first time in fourteen months, offers to fix him and make him forget, and warns that the folded tether "will unfold." Caleb names Susmithaa, refuses ("I'd rather be scared"), and deliberately heads away from the south-east pull toward the woman so he won't lead the program to her. He hides in a steel storm culvert in a drainage cut, where the Crown goes silent. Withdrawal and fourteen months of memory crash in. He recites his victims aloud (the Tartine man, Yuri, Susmithaa), admits he never learned his teammates' names, and vows to keep the canister of Susmithaa's ash until someone "not them" tells him what it is. The two Vesper doses stay untouched in his left pocket.

scenes.title: Dawn Watch
scenes.location: Cross-cut: the East Peak fire road on Mount Tamalpais at 3:01 a.m., and Ava's apartment in the Inner Sunset at 5:48 a.m.
scenes.summary: At 3 a.m. on East Peak, Kino sensed a warmth to the south, beneath the fog, smelling of burnt butter and church. Ix respects it. Kino failed to track it (Survival 6). Nana told him over the phone that he was "shown it" and should bring "the thing you're not saying" to her table at first light. Kino vowed to the Sleeping Lady, "I'll go where you're looking. You don't have to turn around for me." On the way down, the wind fell into step beside him and his cold birthmark briefly eased, a small sign that she has not abandoned him. At 5:48 a.m. in the Inner Sunset, Ava saw a lit flame in her hands in the reflection in her oven glass while her real hands were empty, and her clocks were frozen at 2:41. She tested it scientifically and found it consistent across angles. It gutters when she holds her breath. Behind her reflection she glimpsed another window: a brass lamp, browning marigolds, and an old woman's hand with a ring on the smallest finger that reached to pinch the wick and stopped (Susmithaa's shrine, unnamed to her). She told it, "Don't go out, I've got you." The vision ended with the clocks resetting to 5:52, and an unseen candle-sized warmth now lives in her palms. Her video shows only a deniable smear of light, and a blank phantom calendar reminder for 3:20 a.m. appeared, the minute Amma called Arenya.

scenes.title: Nana's Table
scenes.location: Nana's kitchen, Daly City: stucco house on the hill above Mission St
scenes.summary: At first light Kino confesses to Nana Itzel that he has dreamed the Sleeping Lady rolling away from him since September and hid it. She already knew. The overturned second cup belonged to Susmithaa Sowri, her friend of eleven years (Thursday tea, too much sugar). Nana felt her die at about 2:45 a.m. and turned the cup over. The "butter and church" smell Kino tracked was ghee and camphor: Susmithaa's passing. Nana reframes the dream: the Lady isn't turning from Kino, she's turned toward a "door," and the light went through it to Susmithaa's unbelieving niece. Kino works through his jealousy aloud ("even if it should've been me") and decides a champion stands beside the door, not in front of it. Nana answers that his gift is night-eyes, which is what a lamp needs, and plans to bring pozole to the Sowri house at two with Kino carrying the pot, in a black shirt, saying nothing. She tells him what "wrong" looks like: someone nobody remembers inviting (made forgettable), the memorial lamp's flame leaning toward someone with no draft, and anyone watching the niece "like they're working out how heavy she is." Ix will stay out in the fog past the porch light.

scenes.title: Seton
scenes.location: Seton Medical Center, Daly City — the family room off the ER, before dawn
scenes.summary: At Seton before dawn, Arenya comforts her mother, who brought Susmithaa's cracked brass lamp and refused to give it up. She hides the cold coin-mark on her wrist with a "steering wheel" excuse while Abernathy warns her that the man at the nurses' station has no light at all, "like a hole in a fence." Malachi introduces himself as "Shawani, Department of Energy," apologizes, and waits in the corridor while Arenya takes ten minutes with her family. Amma recalls Susmithaa's last dinner: her Thursday friend Itzel in Daly City will come with pozole if she dies. Appa (Ravi) reveals that in March Susmithaa warned him to deny any niece to an American who came asking. In the corridor, Malachi and Arenya trade: she shows him the wrist mark (he's never seen one and warns her off doctors and photographs); he says Adonis Quinn was Monolith's founder's cousin, that his "people" are three analysts and a phone, that a polite American asked for Susmithaa by full name at about 3:40 a.m., before the paperwork, and that Susmithaa did not die like the nine freeze victims. Arenya gives him her burner number; he'll call once tomorrow. She takes custody of Susmithaa's phone (it buzzed repeatedly at 3 a.m. and once at dawn). The lamp stays warm to her touch, and her right fist begins to loosen for the first time.

scenes.title: Pozole
scenes.location: The Sowri family home, Daly City, 2 p.m. the same day
scenes.summary: At 2 p.m. Nana Itzel and Kino bring pozole to the Sowri house. Arenya and Kino meet for the first time. The memorial lamp's flame leans toward Kino as he passes, then trembles between him and Arenya; Nana's verdict is "not only you." A forgettable Lattice watcher who calls himself "Mr. Bell" (grey cardigan, wearing a frost Crown-fragment) appraises Arenya's warm right hand. He notes that Susmithaa's copy of *Curtain* is upside down and leaves a sealed sympathy card. Ix tracks him to a beige rental Camry (plate 7K…R), where he takes off the Crown, bleeds from the nose and makes a reluctant phone report. Abernathy sees a frost-thread tracking tag on the card, so Nana wraps it in her pot towel and hides it in the freezer ("cold hides in cold"). Inside *Curtain*, Arenya finds a March temple receipt for a prayer in her name, with Susmithaa's note: "Ari — The lamp knows who. Itzel knows the rest. Don't let them count you. Keep your hands still until you can't. Then don't." When Arenya holds it, the lamp flame splits in two for one second. Nana explains *los que cuentan* ("the ones who count") and that Susmithaa's light ran down the maternal line and chose Arenya in March. Arenya confesses the truth to Amma, and Kino shows his cold birthmark and accepts the shared door. Amma keeps everyone the night. The scene ends as Susmithaa's phone shows 14 missed calls from Unknown and a new voicemail at 6:12 p.m.

scenes.title: Fourteen Missed Calls
scenes.location: Sowri family home, Daly City: front room by the memorial lamp, evening
scenes.summary: Arenya unlocked Susmithaa's phone with Appa's birthday and played the 6:12 p.m. voicemail on speaker. The caller was "Daniel Hale, Meridian Mutual Life, beneficiary services." He pronounced "Sowri" exactly as the family does, knew the time of death to the minute (3:19 a.m., which the hospital never gave), and asked to "verify the beneficiary in person" (claim ref MM-031944). Kino saw the lamp flame duck small and blue on the word "her," and his birthmark pulsed. Amma says Susmithaa never mentioned insurance; Appa is evasive. Nana recalled Susmithaa saying in March, "I bought a door, and I put Ari's name on it." Kino failed to spot what Ix was watching, but heard a car pull away dark. Then the Sowri landline rang. Hale left a second message addressed to Arenya: the policy is real, paid in cash at a Colma office on March 19; meet tomorrow at noon at Serramonte Library, second floor by the periodicals, or he'll "come to you." He signed off with "Keep that hand warm," which links him to Mr. Bell. Under his voice, a second voice was counting "eleven, twelve," stopping on "hand." Kino heard it, and Arenya unconsciously wrote it in her margin. Frost formed on the freezer seal where the phone and tracking card are hidden. Nana explained that they count the ones who carry, and saying the number aloud means they've moved from hunting to collecting: "Twelve is you." Everyone sleeps at the Sowri house under the lamp. Ix went alone to scout Serramonte. Arenya has decided nobody goes to the meeting yet; she wants to check the Colma office.

scenes.title: What Ix Brought Back
scenes.location: Sowri house, front room, Daly City (small hours)
scenes.summary: Ravi gave Arenya the three papers Susmithaa left: the Meridian Mutual "welcome" letter numbering her 11 and Arenya 12, her notarized torn NO, and a farewell note. The note said "Writing is not keeping," don't sign, verify or give your full name in a room they chose, and asked Arenya to feed Kino, apologize to Amma about the will, and make Itzel tell the frightening parts. Nana Itzel revealed el Contador, a fair, never-erring clerk-spirit born of the 1912 removal of SF's dead to Colma and the stone-yard shed ledgers. Grey "beneficiary" men read its books and collect. In March she witnessed Susmithaa's salt-and-candle no under the shed door. It was entered, and it bought seven months: "a no buys time, not freedom." A second mark in the salt, two strokes side by side, means dos testigos: a contested entry stays open until two stand for it. Arenya told Kino that if it comes to that she'd want it to be him, and he accepted, though not tonight. Hale's calls are understood as pressure to make her name herself. The landline is unplugged, nobody goes to Serramonte at noon, and the plan is breakfast, then Colma in daylight, with Kino walking the stone yard first and Arenya at the gate. In the bond, Abernathy honestly found his memory of "Mark it so it can be found again" walled off clean, "like somebody tidied up after me." The sun mark in Arenya's palm sank back. The family slept together under the lamp while Nana kept watch.

scenes.title: The Stone Yard
scenes.location: A monument-carving yard off Mission Road, Colma, mid-morning
scenes.summary: At the Esposo Monument Co. yard in Colma, Kino walked first with permission ("Con permiso, vengo a ver, no a tomar") while Arenya stayed at the gate with Nana. The yard is a ruled ledger page. Twelve rows of granite blanks run to the shed, which stands as the heading, and a margin file of blanks lines the left fence. Row 11's margin holds Susmithaa's old salted chisel stroke (her contested March no). Row 12's margin stone is polished and holds a single pencil stroke, a witness of one, waiting for a second. At the shed wall Kino heard el Contador, the same dry counting voice from Hale's voicemail, reading back "Doce. Testigo: una. Falta una." It then silently asked him "¿Y tú?" Kino wanted badly to say yes. He refused to answer by word or gesture, turned his gaze to Arenya to mean "not mine to give," and backed away. The clerk followed his look to Arenya and made a tick: referred. A pencil dot now sits beside the rule under the 12 in Arenya's palm, marked "come back to this." Abernathy confirmed the hot-brass smell returned for half a second at the gate, and the clerk ruled him a blank "not yet" line. Leaving, they saw Mr. Bell's empty beige Camry (7K…) parked across Mission Road with a validation slip from Colma Notary & Mail, likely the "Colma office" of the March 19 policy. Tito Boy remarked on "a lot of visitors" this week.

scenes.title: Two Doors from the Florist
scenes.location: Mission Road, Colma: the drive, then Colma Notary & Mail
scenes.summary: Arenya and Kino entered Colma Notary & Mail, two doors from the florist, while Nana Itzel kept watch from the Corolla. Kino confirmed in the car that the counting voice at the shed was the same dry count as the voicemail, older than Hale, and they agreed no witness decision today. Notary Rodel Panganiban recognized Susmithaa in Arenya ("You have her chin"). On March 19 he notarized Susmithaa's declaration, witnessed by Ravi: she bought nothing, named nobody, and her niece is party to "no contract, no agreement, no understanding," written three ways because "It's not for California." She told him to make anyone who asked about that day write it down. An hour later a polite man in a suit (Hale) rented Box 112 as "Meridian Mutual Services," paying a year in new twenties. That box was left ajar this Wednesday morning as bait, holding a cream envelope "TO THE BENEFICIARY, to be collected in person, ID required." Abernathy smelled hot brass from the box and heard the green thumbprint journal "tick." Mr. Bell had filed a signed journal-copy request for 03/19 that morning ("W. BELL," purpose "Verification of beneficiary," a Daly City PO box), and his handshake left Rodel's palm cold. Arenya photographed the envelope without touching it: on her phone the window shows her real full name. At Nana's two-honk signal they left calmly. Mr. Bell bought a single white chrysanthemum and walked into the notary, and its brass bell didn't ring for him.

scenes.title: Read It Twice
scenes.location: Nana Itzel's kitchen, Daly City, on the hill above Mission St. Wednesday, just past noon.
scenes.summary: In Nana Itzel's kitchen, Kino read the photographed bait envelope twice. On the second read a frost-written line appeared, meant only for whoever reads it aloud: "c/o the one who reads this to her." He refused to say it aloud and take the "job," wrote it down for Nana instead, and Arenya chose not to look ("looking is verifying"), pinning the phone face-down under the salt shaker. Their timeline on the legal pad found the hole: Arenya was entered as "12" because on Sunday, March 8, Susmithaa had an archana said at the Livermore temple in Arenya's name and birth star, the day before the Meridian letter. The freezer turned out to be a "post office": the Ziploc holding Mr. Bell's card and Kino's note frosted shut. It is now buried in salt on the counter, which greyed to the top by 2:15. They agreed that Kino will carry only his own note to the ocean at the Pacifica pier at the 4:50 low tide, and that Bell's card will wait for Malachi to deliver. Kino's trash-run read part of the beige Camry's plate (7K, B or 8, a gap, 4, R; SERRAMONTE AUTO dealer frame). Meanwhile Nana found an ankle-height frost ledger-line ruled across the one unsalted door, the garage side door. They blocked that door with a dresser ("count furniture"). Ix stared pointedly at the line's anchor, the PG&E gas meter. At 3:30 they left together in the Corolla.

scenes.title: Your Own Letter
scenes.location: Pacifica Municipal Pier, Sharp Park. Wednesday, about 4:30 p.m., tide going out.
scenes.summary: At the 4:50 low tide on Pacifica Pier, Kino gave his own note to the sea ("Nana didn't fail. They knew."). It was accepted like a posted letter, and his forearm has stayed warm since: he's out of el Contador's pull for now. Daniel Hale was waiting on Nana's bench, knew her name without being told, and answered Arenya's and Kino's narrow questions truthfully. Susmithaa's March 8 Livermore archana made the entry (she asked for Arenya to be "kept"). Hale rented Box 112 fifty-nine minutes after her declaration. Her single stroke expires on her sixteenth-day rite, when the entry closes as written and Mr. Bell, who filed for "verification of beneficiary," collects; Bell could verify through the notary journal. Hale carries a "real" envelope that would close it "in her favor, you receive" (the trap is that receiving means being kept), and says the box stays open until Friday 7:40. He named a second route besides a witness stroke: un-say the archana in the same temple room, but beware other listeners there. Arenya refused his question about what her aunt carried and put "I don't agree" on his record. Kino reflexively thanked Hale and felt a small "receipt" noted on his birthmark, which he confessed to Arenya. Hale left on ruler-even footsteps that end at an empty parking space. Nana resolved to make pozole for the sixteenth day, and they drove home planning Livermore next.

scenes.title: Thirteen Days
scenes.location: Across the Bay Area, Wednesday night into Thursday morning
scenes.summary: Wednesday night, Malachi's voicemail to Arenya was cut mid-message by el Contador ("…doce. Leído."), and a dry tally stroke appeared on his car's back window. He ditched his phones and texted from a second burner. Arenya answered without naming a place ("Where I got the footage. Opening. Outside, by the bench."); the text wasn't entered, and her pencil dot warmed. Malachi botched the plate read off a reflection in his photo (nat 1): he ran the mirrored plate through a CHP contact, got "never issued," and left his own name and badge number in a CHP query log. Thursday 7:00 a.m. at Tartine, Malachi left a pencilled napkin on the bench (plate fragment 7K?4R, Serramonte Auto frame, "don't call me, I'll find you," "let someone else hold your pen") and walked off phoneless. Mr. Bell then joined the line with a white chrysanthemum. The door chime stayed silent for him, he gave off no breath and the steam bent around him, and the oven flame leaned away. The group refused his "account." He paid in exact change including a 1912 dime (Kino bagged it), read Ava's name off her apron tag (she now has a two-centimetre cold spot on her left palm), and left the chrysanthemum as "a reservation, for the sixteenth day. I understand there will be pozole." Ava stayed on shift with salt in her apron. Arenya and Kino left by the front door. Bell stayed seated at the corner table, unfollowing, apparently knowing they'll return.

scenes.title: Guerrero Street
scenes.location: Sidewalk outside Tartine Bakery, Guerrero and 18th, Thursday ~7:20 a.m.
scenes.summary: Outside Tartine, under a laundromat awning, Arenya and Kino set the morning's rules: they won't return on Bell's schedule, they'll go nameless, and they'll chase the only signed thing they have, the Camry's Serramonte Auto dealer frame, posing as car shoppers ("Joe" and an unnamed buyer). Arenya said her row-twelve options out loud: a second witness (only someone who already stands in it) or un-saying the archana in Livermore before Hale's "other listeners". She is leaning toward Livermore after the Camry lead, and she'll tell Kino first at 7:39. Kino insisted she won't enter the temple room alone; Nana and/or Kino will go with her. Bell's 1912 dime began sweating a dime-sized ring through Kino's coffee sleeve. Abernathy says it is "answering", a spent marker that Bell uses as a window. It's now wrapped in Arenya's scarf and the napkin, carried away from skin, and must not be thrown in the bay. Ava set up a pastry check-in code. On BART past Glen Park the palm dot and the dime both went quiet (out of range). Ava texted that Bell left without eating, took nothing, and left a tip. They reached Nana's house in Daly City around 8 a.m., where Nana is roasting chiles for the pozole.

scenes.title: Cal
scenes.location: Nana Itzel's kitchen, Daly City, Thursday ~8:00 a.m.
scenes.summary: At Nana Itzel's kitchen Thursday morning, Kino dropped Mr. Bell's 1912 dime face down into Nana's cal. It hissed and left a grey ring, and Nana saw a knit-cuff print in it: Bell leaning on the window to the last. The dime is now blind and dead, and that cal is spoiled for the pozole. Arenya's second-witness palm dot then woke, pointing not at the frost-lined garage door but at Nana's dresser. Nana opened the top drawer herself. Inside, Susmithaa's red Brooke Bond Thursday tea tin (camphor, almond-jasmine lotion) held a second declaration signed "S. Sowri," with the witness line left blank: "WITNESS — ITZEL R. MARTÍNEZ." Nana confessed this was the part she left out. Susmithaa asked her to witness in March, and she stalled for months because her name in the book would be Kino's address. Arenya took the paper folded, refused to ask Nana to sign ("I'm not going to go looking for a second in the people who love me"), and keeps it unopened in her notebook. Kino promised to stand beside Nana if she ever chooses to. Nana turned the Guadalupe to watch the garage door, sent Kino to Mi Tierra for Morelos cal and tortillas, and made Arenya eat. The palm dot is now a quiet, keeping warmth.

scenes.title: Dealer Frame
scenes.location: Mi Tierra market, Daly City → Serramonte Auto, Serramonte Blvd., Colma line
scenes.summary: Posing nameless as "Joe Ramos" and his girlfriend, Kino and Arenya worked Benny Benasaraf at Serramonte Auto. Benny told them the beige Camry was sold in March for cash to "Walter Bell": an old man in a cardigan who counted folded bills in Spanish, signed with a fountain pen, read every page twice, and washed out of his Polaroid. His address is Box 12 at Colma Notary & Mail on Mission, the same shop as Hale's Box 112. Bell had phoned Benny last week asking him to take the names of anyone asking about the car; the pair left without giving theirs, and Benny was seen on the phone afterward, eyeing the corkboard. After a decoy stop at the Honda lot they walked to Colma's Mission Street, failed to spot the pollen-dusted Camry parked at the florist, and found it only in the notary's window reflection, a faceless grey-cuffed figure in the driver's seat watching the shop door. Arenya's pencil dot went hot; she called "Civic" and they retreated, but she read the plate from the reflection (7KBQ4R plus one character hidden by a USPS sign). The reflected head turned a beat late to where she had stood. Rodel came out and swept the sidewalk, putting himself between the door and the curb. From the corner, Kino's birthmark pull was cut clean, the Camry's seat was empty with no door opened, and one chrysanthemum in the florist's bucket had turned to face them. They took refuge in Lupe's diner with no way to call Malachi, and the waitress poured a third coffee "for your friend, he said he'd be right in." Its steam bent.

scenes.title: The Third Cup
scenes.location: Lupe's diner, Mission Street, Colma
scenes.summary: At Lupe's diner in Colma, Bell's prepaid third coffee leaned its steam toward the window, then bent around Kino and read Arenya's open notebook until she closed it. Malachi confessed he isn't DOE and that his plate query has left a traceable wake back to his badge. He confirmed 7KBQ4R as a real string to pass through a lawyer or clerk, and named Nana's freezer as the only safe "post office." Lupe passed on Bell's message ("back when it's cold, don't clear it") and gave Arenya a free guest check: "3 COF." with a single pencil stroke in the SERVER box. It was Bell offering himself as her second witness, and her palm dot pulled hard toward it. Kino warned that the clerk would count Bell's hand. Arenya refused aloud ("No"), didn't touch the check with her skin, and pocketed it folded in a napkin as evidence. After her no, the steam rose straight again and Lupe concluded "he's not coming back." They left one at a time: Kino first to Ix, Arenya second, Malachi out the kitchen side uphill toward the cemetery road. Outside, the Camry was gone, leaving a clean pollen rectangle, and one chrysanthemum faced Lupe's door. The check in Arenya's pocket stays faintly warm, a possible window like the dime.

scenes.title: Two Pencils
scenes.location: Colma BART to Nana Itzel's kitchen, Daly City
scenes.summary: At Nana Itzel's kitchen, Arenya set Bell's warm guest check on the table, and Nana salted it dead. Arenya then asked what witnessing would cost her. Over pozole, Nana explained: El Contador keeps the witness, not the signer, and enters them with their household. Bell then "writes to a counted hand" with monthly offers, each worse than the last; Susmithaa got eleven years of envelopes. Signing would put Kino back in the book as "who sleeps here." Kino confessed that the Lady has had her back to him in his dreams for weeks, turned toward Arenya, and chose to go back in anyway: "we'll burn them in the sink." Nana signed the witness line of Susmithaa's second declaration with two strokes (dos testigos). The garage frost melted, Bell's pencil stroke on the check snapped under the salt, and Arenya's palm now shows 12, a rule, and two graphite strokes, cool and without pull. The declaration, read aloud as call and response, reveals that Susmithaa had the March 8 Livermore archana done in Arenya's name ("Ari") with her star and gotra, and that "the priest who read it was not our priest." Nana's ruling: the two-stroke no stands in Colma (the account reads "disputada," so Bell can only wait), but it doesn't reach the Livermore temple. Nana produced check carbon No. 2207 ($101, Mar 8, "for Ari"); the bank's endorsement may name whoever cashed it. Arenya and Kino leave for Livermore by daylight with salt in their pockets, Ix stays with Nana, and Arenya means to call Ava first.

scenes.title: Altamont
scenes.location: Daly City to Livermore, I-580 over the Altamont Pass
scenes.summary: On I-580 over the Altamont Pass, Arenya called Ava at Tartine and told her the truth: she had used her as bait, and she was sorry. Ava said the cold spot on her palm went warm around nine last night, the moment Nana signed. She'll keep the salt and the pastry code (croissant = fine, kouign-amann = call me) and declined the spare bed but wants the address by text. The call dropped at the summit as Ava began asking about the grey cardigan. One turbine blade on the ridge lagged out of step and caught up "like something glancing back." Kino read it as a Bell window, not a door, and told her not to stare. Kino refused to call Ava bait: "you used a door, and she was standing in it." Told the truth afterward, she becomes a lookout. Ava's delayed text arrived on the downslope ("okay. salt tonight. kouign-amann if anything"), and Arenya sent the street address with "salt on the sill." After a gas stop they reached the Livermore temple at 9:20. Arenya's palm was cool and quiet, and Kino's birthmark was still. The office door (ARCHANA / DONATIONS / RECEIPTS, 9–12) stands propped open, with yearly ledger binders on the shelf and an older woman in a blue cardigan at the desk.

scenes.title: The Receipt Book
scenes.location: Temple office, Livermore hills
scenes.summary: At the Livermore temple, Sastri performed a closing rite over the March 8 archana done in Arenya's name, naming her only as "ayam," this one. A planted flip phone imitated Amma's voice to make Arenya speak her name. She held silent (DC 14 Wis save, 19), and Kino folded the phone against his chest. He now carries a phone-shaped numb cold rectangle over his sternum, and the dead phone showed Rodel's Colma Notary & Mail number. The register's March 8 entry, No. 2207, $101, archana for "Ari" with Susmithaa's star and gotra, was signed by a "visiting Pt. H. Dalal, Fremont" with a ruler-straight hooked line, and listed Rodel's phone and "c/o Colma Notary & Mail, Box 112", eleven days before Hale rented that box. The check was never deposited: the visitor took it himself as dakshina "per family," so the endorsement image lives on Susmithaa's bank statement, which Amma handles. Arenya refused to finish copying the signature; one bracket-hook stays in her notebook, inert but making the cover feel heavier. Kino found grey hairlines in every third grout seam, stopping at the sanctum threshold, because the visitor wore shoes and never passed the lamp. The pair left for food, planning to see Amma or Appa in person tonight about the statement.

scenes.title: Paper Dosa
scenes.location: A South Indian lunch counter off First Street, downtown Livermore, late afternoon
scenes.summary: At a South Indian lunch counter off First Street in Livermore, Arenya and Kino made a twenty-minute truce: no names, no numbers, no writing. Kino rated the cold, phone-shaped patch on his sternum a "three, maybe four." He confessed that at nine, during his night alone on the mountain, nothing came to sit with him, and he lied to Nana that a deer had. Arenya confessed that part of her is glad something real is finally happening, and ashamed of it, and that part of her keeps "taking notes." As she said it, her notebook grew briefly heavier under her hand, like something answering to its name. Kino saw this and said nothing. Arenya told him that he was the deer: he stayed all night. Kino told her taking notes is how she stays a person, "just don't let it sign anything." The counter man kept feeding Kino unasked. They left for Daly City to confront Amma about Susmithaa's bank statement and the 2207 endorsement. Arenya will ask, and Kino will watch Amma's hands.

scenes.title: The Statement
scenes.location: Sowri family home, Daly City: the kitchen, late afternoon
scenes.summary: In the Daly City kitchen, Amma (Lakshmi) gave up the hidden folder. The back of Susmithaa's check 2207 bears a forged "R. Sowri" in the visitor's ruler-straight hooked hand, then "Pay to the order of H. Dalal." She had hidden it from Appa after he told her "It's handled." A gas meter in the side yard frosted from the inside, ran a ruler frost line to the garage door handle, and its dials read 2207 while one tick added a stroke of weight to Arenya's shut notebook. Kino's sternum patch ticked with it and his heart slipped further behind (now about a 4). Nobody took the "receipt," so the needles returned to Appa's ordinary 4471 and the frost line snapped. Appa's meter book, wedged by the pipe, held his torn 3:12 p.m. entry, "Ari does not sign." Appa (Raghavan) came home with Susmithaa's red-string side-door key and confessed. In March a flat-voiced American posing as the temple asked whether the family approved giving the dakshina to the visiting pandit, and Appa said "Whatever my sister wants is fine." Rodel the notary, who owed Susmithaa for nine nights at his dying mother's bedside, later told Appa to hold her key, that "things that count come in where things are counted," and to write the family's no where the meter reads. Rodel also said "he asked me for one-twelve before it was empty." Amma laid the key at the foot of the lamp, the family ate together, and they agreed to question Rodel in daylight on Friday morning, before Box 112 closes at 7:40, with Appa driving.

scenes.title: One-Twelve, Before It Was Empty
scenes.location: Colma Notary & Mail, Mission Road — Friday, 7:25 a.m.
scenes.summary: Friday 7:25 at Colma Notary & Mail, Rodel showed Arenya and Kino his private blue BOX RENTALS ledger. Box 112 had been Susmithaa's for eleven years, and Bell's Box 12 left long unstamped envelopes in it every March. In late February a faceless man, "Mr. Dalal from Fremont," came in person, knew her star, borrowed Rodel's phone number "for the paperwork," and had Rodel pencil "Hold 112 for Mr. Dalal on vacancy" in Rodel's own pencil. The hand was ruler-straight with the bracket-hook, written through him. Susmithaa emptied and closed 112 on March 6 ("they're moving in next door to me"). Arenya's phone camera showed an unwritten sum-rule under the pencil line and a hidden child-style sun after Susmithaa's box-closing signature. Hale's instructions came through a flat 0:41 call at 9:12 the night before. The caller said Arenya's full name and told Rodel to offer coffee and ask only for ID. Arenya refused the box, the ID and the coffee, and had Rodel write in his own slant "Declined. Nothing accepted. — R.P." with no second hand. The 112 keyhole stopped shimmering, and the pen was left uncapped across the page. Kino salted the alley sill, and they left by the side door to Appa's car. At exactly 7:40 Hale stepped out of the grey Nissan that had sat empty since before six. He collected the cream envelope, nodded toward their hidden car, and drove toward Colma. Rodel texted that he refused Hale tea ("Not today"), closed 112 and ordered a new lock.

scenes.title: The Long Way on 280
scenes.location: Appa's Camry, I-280 south from Colma, Friday morning
scenes.summary: At the Serramonte Chevron, while Appa stalled at the coffee machines to give them time, Kino ended his silence. He told Arenya her notebook grows heavier when she says something true aloud, answering to her rather than to the Lady or Nana, and that for weeks the Lady has turned her back to him in his mountain dreams. Kino argued Hale is a "form" something fills, since the Nissan stayed warm with no one breathing, and that Hale read their position from Rodel's book. Everything written is a place they can be found, and someone moved up Bell's March calendar out of impatience. Arenya offered that a dog turning its back in a doorway is guarding, not ignoring. Then she confessed she and Saiesh cloned Teddy's keycard and requested the Tartine footage under his credentials, "his name, my hand," which mirrors Dalal's method. She wrote "7:58. Told Kino the truth. Nothing signed for anyone else." The line came out darker, as if pressed from the other side, and her numb left palm turned warm with one pulse: a count she placed herself. Kino urged her to tell Teddy tonight, before someone with a pen does. Appa returned, revealed the thermos held Amma's rasam warmed at five, asked only whether it went okay, drank a capful Arenya offered ("too much pepper," his voice catching), and turned up her heater instead of answering about "it's handled." Past Crystal Springs, where the palm marks had previously gone quiet, the warm spot stayed, traveling with her.

scenes.title: Before Someone With a Pen
scenes.location: Fri Oct 30, late morning → evening: the Sowri house, then San Francisco
scenes.summary: Friday evening. Arenya confessed to Teddy in person at the office: she cloned his keycard and made up the "Urban Mortality Patterns" DPH footage request. Teddy took her keycard until Monday, insisted they write the DPH letter together with legal, and refused to sign anything for anyone. A reception slip showed a nameless man had called asking whether Teddy had "signed for it yet," leaving Rodel's number. Then Teddy's desk phone dialed Rodel's number by itself and rang out into a 0:41 voicemail (the same length as the temple flip-phone call). Arenya's warm palm pulsed once. Teddy unplugged the phone, and the voicemail is to be heard Monday with legal. Meanwhile Malachi watched Benny at Serramonte Auto lie about the Camry buyer and speed-dial someone. At Nana's, Kino looked past the Lady in a dream: she is standing between him and a ruled grey line that tick-counts his steps, and something at its far end felt him look. At Tartine, Caleb Strand showed himself to Malachi and Ava. His canister of Susmithaa's ash synced to Ava's palm ache while the corner table was in sight. He confessed he was "One," the grey jacket who sat at the corner table during Yuri Melnikov's death, and on the team that took Susmithaa Monday. He named Dorsey, Pruitt and a "Four, Hale" whose neck turns like a camera mount (in his account not the notary Hale). He says his "Crown" went dark Monday and he has refused the Vesper. Ava logged it all at 7:14 and set a meeting in Tartine's back room at 9:00, where Arenya and Kino are now arriving to hear Caleb's confession.

scenes.title: The Back Room
scenes.location: Tartine Bakery, back room (Guerrero & 18th, San Francisco)
scenes.summary: Caleb Strand confessed in Tartine's back room. Monday in Daly City, Susmithaa was at her sink holding Arenya's old blue mug with its half-peeled cartoon-bird sticker. She asked "Can I help you?", then looked past him toward the city and said a two-sound name he can't recall (maybe "kanna"). The Crown tagged it "proximal reference logged." Caleb admitted the lift felt good. He said his one unordered choice was knotting her tether so nothing could follow it to Arenya. Shepherd is only a polite voice heard through the Crown. Drop Two is a Peninsula lot with a roll-up door where a man with a backwards lanyard signs canisters into a white van. Caleb stole Susmithaa's ash canister rather than deliver it, and he warned that Shepherd scheduled something for "Friday," which is tonight. When Arenya laid her hand on the duffel, the canister synced to her pulse and then settled. The room smelled of Aunty's filter coffee and cold cream, Ava's cold palm cleared completely, and Abernathy felt a warm presence sit on the bond without noticing him. Malachi admitted he isn't with the Department of Energy and told of an identical port-city death eleven years ago that ended at the same kind of lot. He suspects his own employers trained Caleb's team, and he promised the name of who he works for later. Nana Itzel agreed to take the ash and to let Caleb sleep on her porch behind her salt. Leaving, the group found the grey Nissan at the alley's 18th Street end: plate 7KBQ4R2, a backwards lanyard on the mirror, and fog on the passenger window that drew four tally strokes from inside and paused over a fifth. They left by Guerrero and drove south on Mission toward Excelsior, Kino's truck ahead and Malachi with Caleb a block behind. The ash rode in Arenya's lap.

scenes.title: Behind Her Salt
scenes.location: Nana Itzel's house, Hillcrest, Daly City (hill above Mission St)
scenes.summary: Friday night into Saturday Oct 31 at Nana Itzel's in Hillcrest. Nana laid her salt line; Kino told her the Lady stands outside it, facing west, and Nana told him a turned back guards the house. Arenya was invited across with a pinch of salt and set Susmithaa's canister on Nana's ofrenda shelf beside Ernesto. Caleb crossed on Nana's word to the glider, and Kino closed the line. Lamps died up the hill; the empty grey Nissan (7KBQ4R2) rolled up with no engine; the cottage light came on and a looping voice said "Can I help you?", then called "Kanna?" — the Crown's logged last word. Arenya held (Wis save 20) and the canister answered her with two ticks and warmth; Abernathy says that was the warm presence, not a copy, and that he felt himself "counted and dropped" when the fifth stroke on the Nissan's glass started and stopped unfinished. The car rolled away, lamps returning behind it. Caleb laid down his Vesper packs unopened; Kino's sternum ache is gone. At dawn Malachi (Inv 18) found a weightless dry rectangle at the curb, leather-soled prints of a man who stood all night, a clipboard corner on Susmithaa's gate, a pink carbon scrap "…CEIVED BY:" (blank; told only to Arenya), and a lamp humming four-and-a-half. Caleb's dead prepaid, wrapped under Nana's clay comal, showed an 11:14 PM text: "LOST PROPERTY — CUSTODY CHAIN INCOMPLETE. RECEIPT TO BE COUNTERSIGNED BY NEXT OF KIN. SIGNATORY ON FILE: R. SOWRI. SUN 11/1. WE WILL COME TO HIM." Caleb recalls R. Sowri on Monday's clipboard. Nana sends Malachi to drive Arenya home in daylight, no phones, with a twist of salt for Appa's step and a message: Raghavan came to her porch in March and wouldn't come in, and he can stop being brave alone now. Kino stays with Nana and Caleb behind the salt.

scenes.title: It's Handled
scenes.location: Sowri family home, Daly City — kitchen door, Saturday Oct 31, ~8:00 a.m.
scenes.summary: Saturday Oct 31, ~8:00 a.m., at the Sowri kitchen door in Daly City. Arenya poured Nana's salt on the swept step next to Kino's line, slid the green Sheaffer away from a sealed, unpostmarked envelope addressed "R. SOWRI — NEXT OF KIN," and asked Appa who handed him the pen in March. Appa confessed. On March 19 at Rodel's counter, Rodel's chained ballpoint skipped, and a polite man in a navy coat holding a mailbox key (Hale, who rented Box 112 an hour later) offered his pen cap-first. Appa wrote the "R" of his witness signature in that man's ink before Susmithaa took the pen back ("we have our own"). She steadied Appa's wrist while he finished "Sowri" in his own Sheaffer. So the signature on her declaration is half theirs, the source of "SIGNATORY ON FILE: R. SOWRI." Since March he has had a cold grey pencil-lead stain on his right forefinger and thumb. The envelope was left at 5 a.m. along a ruled line of grey dust, which he swept. He had planned to sign alone on Sunday so Arenya wouldn't have to. Arenya and Kino argued that signing would close the custody chain for them, and Arenya delivered Nana's message. Appa admitted that in March he refused to cross Nana's threshold so his family wouldn't be written in as household, then stepped over both salt lines. The kitchen landline rang once, then once again, like counting, and nobody answered. The envelope rides unopened under Nana's blanket and salt in Kino's truck. Malachi found leather-soled prints and a dry car-shaped rectangle at the curb, and on the side gas meter, fog-writing that read "R.S. — SUN 9:00" before it faded. Everyone is driving together to fetch Amma from temple.

scenes.title: Saturday Seva
scenes.location: Small Hindu temple in a converted church off El Camino Real, San Bruno: shoe rack, hall, back kitchen
scenes.summary: Saturday ~8:45–9:20 a.m., San Bruno temple (a converted Lutheran church). In the vestibule, a pair of size 10–11 black oxfords sat toes-out with grey ruled-line dust packed in the welt, and Ix confirmed "pencil." In the back kitchen Amma introduced "Dalal-ji" of Fremont, the Livermore second-Sunday archana priest and the H. Dalal on check 2207's endorsement. He wore black dress socks and kept a blue ballpoint behind his ear. He mentioned Susmithaa's $101 March archana for Arenya. Arenya refused seat, pen and receipt ("we have our own"). Malachi stood between him and the family, Kino blocked the propped back door, and Amma turned off the flame and told Dalal in Tamil she knew he'd cashed the check and the endorsement wasn't Raghavan's hand. Dalal laid his pen flat, cap toward himself, and said he keeps names, not boxes. He said he speaks names to God, that "God has many ears in this country; some of them pay." He warned that someone "who does not know the words" will come to the side door at 9:00 Sunday with a pen, and offered himself as one who does know them. Kino and Malachi recovered the shoes without touching the oxfords. In Amma's left Clark was a pink archana slip in blue ballpoint: "LAKSHMI SOWRI · ROHINI · SAT 10/31 · PAID ✓." Amma did not ask for it, and she handed it flat to Arenya. The family now drives together to Nana's in Hillcrest, with Arenya telling Amma everything and Malachi following.

scenes.title: Since When
scenes.location: Kino's truck, 280 South to Hillcrest, then Nana's kitchen
scenes.summary: On 280 South, Arenya told Amma everything: the nine deaths, the wall, the keycard crime, Susmithaa's March archana, Hale's pen. Amma revealed that Susi had phoned her in March for the family's stars and that she never gave her own, so someone else supplied Rohini. When Amma and Appa said "Susmithaa Sowri" aloud, the cold in the cab drew back into the R. SOWRI envelope. At Nana's gate, under Nana's rules (half on the salt, the non-signing hand, opened with wood), Appa chose to know, and Kino opened it. It was a Shepherd's-crook "Return of Personal Effects — Custody Receipt," REF PROXIMAL/11, for Susmithaa's container "c/o LUCERO, I." It has a pre-written grey pencil R (the March R), "ALTERNATE SIGNATORY: L. SOWRI ✓," a carry-forward clause, and a torn-off pink corner matching Malachi's curb scrap. Abernathy saw a set thread from the R into Appa's stained thumb and a slack thread to Amma's left foot. It went limp when Arenya took off Amma's shoe and sock. The sock burned with pencil-smoke, but the form didn't change ("fire takes the thing, not the writing"), and the form stays on the salt under Nana's pestle. Caleb identified the crook as a runner's book (the office that closes): a polite man who stands vigil at the curb until someone signs, keeps carbon stubs, wears oxfords with grey welt dust and a backward lanyard, and never drives (the Pacifica/Okafor case, SamTrans 110). Appa gave his Sheaffer to Amma, who put it in Nana's salted clay jar. The plan: Kino and Malachi scout the San Bruno temple, its shoe rack and the bus routes this afternoon; Caleb watches the porch; Arenya stays with her parents; and Malachi will tell Amma who he is tonight.

scenes.title: The Long Afternoon
scenes.location: Hillcrest (Nana's) / San Bruno temple and the El Camino bus stops / Tartine, the Mission. Sat Oct 31, 11 a.m. to dusk
scenes.summary: Saturday afternoon, Oct 31. Kino and Malachi found the San Bruno shoe rack empty: the oxfords had been lifted straight up, "collected." A trolley woman told them the runner rides SamTrans 110 on a pink paper transfer that shouldn't exist anymore. Malachi wrapped Dalal's left-behind reading glasses in a handkerchief. At the 110's Daly City BART turnaround (bay C) they found the runner's habitual grey-dust footprints and a grey-pencil "8:12" ticked beside the first Sunday run, which would bring him to Hillcrest in time for the 9:00 meter vigil. At Nana's, the landline rang once at 3:12 and nobody answered. Arenya held Amma's cold left foot all afternoon. Just after five the slack thread's residue released: the cold passed through Arenya's hands to the wrist for three heartbeats and then left both of them, and Nana told her to wash with salt. At Tartine, Ava salted her thresholds, and at 5:58 the oven light swung once toward the southwest (Pacifica) and then settled back south. Caleb held the porch with his scar cool, and at dusk Malachi arrived at Nana's gate, outside the salt, waiting to be invited in to meet Amma.

scenes.title: Hat in Hand
scenes.location: Nana Itzel's house, Hillcrest, Daly City: the gate, the salt line, the kitchen table
scenes.summary: At dusk Malachi waited outside Nana's salt line until Arenya made him say two things at the gate: his real name and who pays him. He is Malachi Shawani, a CIA case officer in a four-person off-book domestic cell, and his team doesn't know about this family. He crossed cleanly, but Dalal's wrapped reading glasses in his pocket greyed a hand's width of the salt. Nana had it covered with fresh salt, not swept, and put the glasses in a lidded blue jar on the top shelf, a hand's width from Susmithaa's canister. The jar made a single pencil-tick sound. In the bond, a fine grey thread now runs from it downhill to the 110 stop. At the table Malachi told Amma everything: an overseas death eleven years ago that he was ordered to forget, nine matching deaths his cell counts here, every clue toward Sunday's 9:00 a.m. visit, and a CHP query on Arenya's car that carries his name. Amma, the ticked alternate signatory, announced she would face the runner herself. Arenya argued her down ("you're the person they ticked the box for"), and Amma agreed to stand behind her, barefoot, with Appa's capped Sheaffer in her pocket. She called Arenya "kanna" again. The plan is set: Kino at the bus shelter by 8:10, Caleb on the glider watching the hill, Malachi at the curb with no pen and no name, Arenya behind the gate, Amma behind her. Nana approved trading the glasses on her terms: the jar goes down on the wooden side of the comal, the family's copy of the form never leaves the house, the runner must strike his own line in his own pencil and say aloud that he's done it, and nobody speaks Susmithaa's name to him.

scenes.title: All Hallows
scenes.location: Nana's house, Hillcrest (Daly City) — Halloween night into Sunday morning; Tartine (Ava)
scenes.summary: Sunday Nov 1, 7:48–9:30 a.m., Hillcrest. Kino watched the 110 arrive at 8:38. The runner stepped off, ticked Kino as "already on the list," and Pt. Dalal followed him, without his glasses, walking inside the runner's grey footprints. Kino salted the sidewalk behind them at the hydrant and the bus left. At bay C, Ava saw the 8:12 tick move to the 9:12. Malachi faced the runner alone at the curb and argued (Persuasion 16 vs DC 15) that the R was written in the issuer's ink, so the entry was opened in error. The runner agreed to void it, but the void needed a witness who keeps names. Dalal took his glasses back off the wooden comal and read whatever faced him. Everyone turned their backs except Malachi. Dalal read Malachi's true name and his past ("forty seconds, a market, someone else wore glasses that day; you have been on a page that is not ours"), read the house as "Lucero," and frowned at a blank page at the kitchen window (Abernathy, hidden in the pantry, felt nothing). The runner struck Proximal eleven and the alternate ("Issuer's ink. Returned up the line. Closed."). The family's copy of the form struck itself, Appa's stain receded to a crescent under the nail, and Caleb's scar went cool. At that moment the fog bank stopped breathing, lifted, and, seen only by Ava, something vast turned over beneath it and lay down farther out to sea. The runner rode the 9:12 back with the balance "on his lap" toward the ink's issuer (Hale's office). Dalal said, "The box was the other man's. I only keep the names." Afterward Caleb confessed in front of Appa that he helped kill Susmithaa. Appa didn't forgive him but told him to sit at the table, not on the floor. Ava arrived with coffee. A palm-sized circle has been wiped in the condensation inside the kitchen window, matching the shelter's, and Kino plans to sit that window alone.

scenes.title: The Window Hour
scenes.location: Nana Itzel's kitchen, Hillcrest, Daly City — Sunday Nov 1, 9:40 a.m.
scenes.summary: Kino sat Nana's kitchen window for an hour (9:40–10:40 a.m., Sun Nov 1) behind a corner-to-corner salt line on the sill, after leaving a small hill of salt as a courtesy in front of the pantry. Arenya and Abernathy watched from a chair behind him, using the reflection in the oven door. At 10:21 the stove clock stopped for eleven seconds in time with the fog's breath, and a long back stayed above the offshore water a moment too long. In the oven-door reflection Arenya saw a forehead-height smudge on the outside of the glass, with no one on the step. A fingertip on the outside drew a waterline and a rising hump, then stopped unfinished like the Nissan's fifth stroke; it wrote no name and spoke no word. Abernathy got the 'blank page' again, closer, felt like he was being waited on, and flinched at the drawing as something he'd seen before but can't place. At the end of the hour the sill line was intact, but the pantry salt hill was gone and the linoleum was clean, as if taken like a gift. Abernathy is sure it was manners, not a debt. Arenya logged times and photographed the circle, sill and clock. Next steps: ask Nana whether taking the salt was manners or a debt, keep the pantry shut, and tell Malachi about the blank page.

scenes.title: Monday
scenes.location: Hillcrest, Daly City → the Mission → the city, Sun night Nov 1 to Mon noon Nov 2
scenes.summary: Monday Nov 2, morning to 1 p.m. The Heron Thing clip (Candlestick, 6:52) goes viral with the 11-second breath; Kino's left forearm warmed 6:52–6:53, keyed to the water, not the bird. Ava's oven swung east at 11:58 Sunday night. Appa's PG&E contact reports Hudson Ave meters and the Sowri block ticked back 11 seconds at 6:52, and Appa adds it to the "11" envelope on the fridge. Nana says the taken salt was manners: the thing now knows it's welcome, so don't leave more unless you mean it. Teddy keeps Arenya on the waterfront beat (600 words due Tue 5 p.m.) with a new keycard, and reveals her old card pinged the Monolith lobby reader twice Saturday while locked in his drawer. Elias confirms the coffee: Wed 6:40, Crissy Field warming hut, "He'll be early. He's always early when he's scared." Malachi saw 3 calls from a 703 number, a buried CHP record, and Corinne's memo (meeting Tue 1 p.m.). At 11:58 Rodel left a message on the landline: Dalal came to his shop with a man in a grey suit who paid for a page from the book, then bought oranges. Malachi's true name has been sold. Abernathy heard a turn signal tick eleven times on the tape. The cassette is in Nana's freezer; Kino salted the hall sill; Malachi will park a block away and keep distance from Arenya. The ofrenda is built with Susmithaa's canister; church at four, Colma after.

Teddy keeps Arenya on the waterfront beat (600 words due Tue 5 p.m.) with a new keycard, and reveals her old card pinged the Monolith lobby reader twice Saturday while locked in his drawer. Elias confirms the coffee: Wed 6:40, Crissy Field warming hut, "He'll be early. He's always early when he's scared." Malachi saw 3 calls from a 703 number, a buried CHP record, and Corinne's memo (meeting Tue 1 p.m.). At 11:58 Rodel left a message on the landline: Dalal came to his shop with a man in a grey suit who paid for a page from the book, then bought oranges. Malachi's true name has been sold. Abernathy heard a turn signal tick eleven times on the tape. The cassette is in Nana's freezer; Kino salted the hall sill; Malachi will park a block away and keep distance from Arenya. The ofrenda is built with Susmithaa's canister; church at four, Colma after.
